today_summary: GCM26 marked $3,886 on the 16 Nov snapshot, dead flat (+$1.0) versus 13 Nov after a $228 five-session slide. The chain is structurally call-heavy — 290,819 call OI against 110,403 put OI (P/C 0.38) — but that skew is legacy far-OTM paper; the live battleground is the rebuilt $3,900 put wall at 6,318 contracts, sitting just $14 above spot. ATM IV 22.52% implies a 1σ daily move of $55 (1.42%) with 9 days to expiry. Reported max pain $5,300 is an artifact of stale 5,500/6,000 call OI rather than a gravity point — the real pin zone is the $3,900–$4,000 corridor.
five_day_thesis: Spot dropped $228.2 (-5.5%) from $4,114 on 10 Nov to $3,886, but the last two sessions printed $3,885 then $3,886 — the slide has stalled flat. The decisive change came on 13 Nov when windowed net GEX flipped positive to negative (+35.8 → -232.6) and it has since deepened to -243.0, so dealers now sit short gamma across the entire ±20% corridor instead of damping moves. The put wall whipsawed $3,700 → $3,500 on 13 Nov and then snapped up to $3,900 on 16 Nov, a +$400 migration that repriced downside protection directly onto spot. The call wall has not budged off $5,500 in all five sessions while ATM IV expanded +1.01pp (21.51% → 22.52%), so premium richened with upside structure untouched. Put OI shed 7,846 contracts into the 9-DTE window against 6,915 calls, dragging P/C OI from 0.41 to 0.38.
